p: it came to pass in those: Christ, the son of God, taking upon himself the form of a servant, and making himself of no reputation, is poorly born in a stable: and by the means of Augustus, the mightiest prince in the world, (thinking nothing of it) has his cradle prepared in Bethlehem, as the prophets foretold.
world should be: As far as the empire of the Romans stretched.

taxed: That is, the inhabitants of every city should have their names recorded, and their goods rated at a certain value, that the emperor might understand how rich every country, city, family, and house was.
city of David: Which David was born and brought up in.
And there were in the same: The angels themselves declare to poor shepherds (not at all regarding the pride of the mighty) the Godhead and office of the child lying in the crib.
abiding in the field: Living outside, and in the open air.
came upon them: Came suddenly upon them, when they were not at all thinking about such a matter.
a multitude of the heavenly host: Whole armies of angels, who compass the majesty of God round about, just as soldiers, as it were.
good will toward men: God's ready, good, infinite, and gracious favour towards men.

And when eight days were accomplished: Christ, the head of the Church, made subject to the law in order to deliver us from the curse of the law (as the name of Jesus well declares) being circumcised, ratifies and seals in his own flesh the circumcision of the flesh.
And when the days of: Christ, upon whom all our sins were laid, being offered to God according to the law purifies both Mary and us all in himself.
her purification according to the law: This is meant for the fulfilling of the law: for otherwise the virgin was not defiled, nor unclean, by the birth of this child.
And: Simeon openly in the temple foretells the death of the coming of Messiah, of the casting out of the greatest part of Israel, and of the calling of the Gentiles.
Holy Ghost was upon him: He was endued with the gifts of the Holy Spirit, and this is said using the figure of speech metonymy.
parents brought in the child Jesus: Joseph and Mary: and he says "parents" because that is what most of the people then thought.
lettest thou thy servant depart in: Let me depart out of this life, to be joined to my Father.
word: As you promised me.
mine eyes have seen thy: That is, for I have seen with my very eyes: for he saw before in mind, as it is said of Abraham, "He saw my day and rejoiced."
salvation: That in which your salvation is contained.
before the face of all people: As a sign set up in a high place for all men to look upon.
set for the: Is appointed and set by God for a mark.
fall and rising again of many: Fall of the reprobate who perishes because of their own fault: and for the rising of the elect, unto whom God will give faith to believe.
sign which shall be spoken against: That is, a mark, which all men will strive earnestly to hit.
pierce through thy own soul also: Will most keenly wound and grieve.
And there was one Anna: Another witness besides Simeon, against whom no objection may be brought, inviting all men to the receiving of the Messiah.
filled with wisdom: As Christ grew up in age, so the virtue of his Godhead showed itself more and more.
Now his parents went to Jerusalem: The scribes and Pharisees are aroused to hear the wisdom of Christ in his time by an extraordinary deed.

And when they saw him: All duties which we owe to men, even though they are not to be neglected, so are they (according to the position in life which God has set us) not to be preferred before the glory of God.
And he went down with them: Christ, very man, is made like us in every way except sin.
